judged_text: The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` each evaluate to a single constant string, so the intended "any property with a number is the expiry" wildcard never exists — the schema degenerates to effectively `{ access_token: string }` and the expiry date the sync contract promises ("The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") is silently discarded. Expiry returned by the sync endpoint is never parsed or persisted, so consumers that rely on expiry_date (e.g. Google's isExpired pre-check) see credentials as perpetually expired and hit the sync endpoint on every request instead of only near expiry.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS this evaluates to a single constant property name (e.g. "ZodString"/"[object Object]"), not a wildcard/index signature. As a result the schema does not model “any numeric property is expiry”; instead it either (a) requires a nonsense constant key and will fail `safeParse` for normal token responses, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw in sync mode, or (b) at best does not reliably parse/persist the expiry field the comment/contract implies. This is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff.
